skill.name: baoyu-danger-x-to-markdown
skill.description: Convert X posts, threads, and articles to Markdown using a TypeScript CLI. It uses reverse-engineered X endpoints and requires explicit consent plus X authentication cookies.
skill.summary: Convert X posts, threads, and articles into Markdown files with source metadata.
skill.author: jimliu

security_audit.summary: The skill is high risk because it launches Chrome with remote debugging, extracts X cookies, stores them locally, and calls private X GraphQL endpoints. Most template-literal and documentation backtick findings are false positives, but the credential, network, filesystem, and command execution behavior is confirmed. Review should focus on cookie handling, executable path control, token logging, and the EXTEND.md override mechanism.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer official OAuth or API flows, avoid Chrome cookie extraction when possible, encrypt local cookie storage, and never log token fragments.
Validate X_CHROME_PATH against a trusted allowlist, or remove the override before launching a browser process.
Remove workflow override support or restrict extensions to declarative settings that cannot change execution or consent behavior.
Document every contacted domain, isolate authenticated requests, and prefer official supported APIs when available.

content.value_statement: Researchers and writers often need durable Markdown copies of X posts, threads, and articles. This skill fetches X content with user-provided authentication and formats it as Markdown.
actual_capabilities: Converts X tweet URLs into Markdown with source metadata.
Fetches multi-post threads and keeps per-post source links.
Extracts X Article content and media references when available.
Writes Markdown to a default folder or a user-selected output path.
Loads X cookies from environment variables or a local Chrome login flow.
limitations: Requires X authentication cookies or an interactive Chrome login.
Uses private X endpoints that may change without notice.
Opens a local Chrome debugging session during browser login.
Cannot guarantee access to protected, deleted, or rate-limited posts.

use_cases.title: Archive Research Threads
use_cases.description: Save public X threads as Markdown notes with source links and media references.

use_cases.title: Prepare Documentation References
use_cases.description: Turn a cited X post or article into a Markdown file for project documentation.

use_cases.title: Collect Social Media Sources
use_cases.description: Create local Markdown records of posts before summarizing or reviewing them.

output_examples.output: A Markdown file with front matter, source URL, author details, post count, and ordered thread sections.
A Markdown article that includes the title, text blocks, and media links when the API returns them.

output_examples.input: A conversion request with a custom output folder.
output_examples.output: The generated Markdown file path inside the chosen folder, with any existing default directory backed up first.

best_practices: Confirm consent before first use and explain the private API risk.
Use only accounts and cookies that the user controls.
Review generated Markdown before sharing captured content.
anti_patterns: Do not run the skill with another person's cookies or account.
Do not archive protected or private content without permission.
Do not depend on the reverse-engineered API as a stable integration.

faq.question: Does this use the official X API?
faq.answer: No. It uses reverse-engineered X web endpoints, so behavior may break or trigger account restrictions.

faq.question: Why does it need cookies?
faq.answer: The private X endpoints require authenticated web session cookies for many post and article requests.

faq.question: Can it convert threads?
faq.answer: Yes. It fetches related thread entries and formats them as ordered Markdown sections.

faq.question: Can it convert X Articles?
faq.answer: Yes, when the endpoint returns article content or article data linked from the tweet.

faq.question: Where does it store data?
faq.answer: It writes Markdown outputs to the chosen folder and can store cookies and consent records in local app data paths.

faq.question: Is it safe for automated use?
faq.answer: Use caution. Automation requires credential handling, private endpoints, and local file storage.
